stories.title: How fast is C++26's std::hive?
stories.dek: Daniel Lemire benchmarks the new C++26 std::hive container against vector and list for append, iteration, erase, and memory use.
stories.why: Lemire measures hive on GCC 16.1 with nanoseconds, cycles, and instructions per element, so you can see exactly where the container's guarantees cost you instead of trusting marketing claims.
stories.takeaway: Hive is not a faster vector — it is a better list: stable references and O(1) scattered erase with only about a byte per element of overhead over a packed vector, but iteration stays latency-bound like a list.

stories.title: Show HN: Kakehashi – Experimental userspace to run macOS binaries on Linux ARM
stories.dek: A userspace translation layer that loads Darwin Mach-O binaries on Linux aarch64 with a freestanding libSystem and BSD syscall translation.
stories.why: For systems engineers curious about running macOS CLI tools (7-Zip, curl) on cheap Linux arm64 CI runners without emulating the CPU — the README includes honest measured performance gaps and a cost comparison against macOS runners.
stories.takeaway: The overhead is at the syscall boundary, not the instructions: multi-file 7zz runs about 5.2x slower under kh, yet Linux arm64 CI minutes cost roughly 10–12x less than macOS, which is the actual motivation.

stories.title: Rooting, firmware analysis and persistent credentials of the TP-Link TL-841N
stories.dek: A hands-on teardown of a $10 router: UART discovery, firmware dumps via tftp and a CH341A flash programmer, squashfs unpacking, and the hardcoded credentials inside.
stories.why: A concrete end-to-end IoT hacking walkthrough demonstrating both firmware extraction routes on a real device, ending with plaintext admin credentials and an unsalted password hash.
stories.takeaway: Even budget consumer routers ship hardcoded admin creds (admin:admin, admin:1234) and unsalted MD5 password hashes in firmware — one credential survives a full factory reset.

stories.title: sizeof is surprisingly difficult to parse in C
stories.dek: Why parsing sizeof's operand is a backtracking trap: compound literals and postfix operators blur the line between type names and expressions.
stories.why: A compact parser-design note for anyone working on C frontends — it covers the naive approach, the compound-literal case like sizeof(int){0}, and why merging cast and unary parsing breaks on sizeof(int)+1.
stories.takeaway: You cannot unify unary-expression and cast parsing for sizeof: sizeof(int)+1 is addition, not the size of a cast — and C2y's new _Countof inherits every one of the same cases.

stories.title: Go 1.27 Interactive Tour
stories.dek: A hands-on, runnable tour of Go 1.27: generic methods, promoted-field struct literals, wider type inference, ML-DSA post-quantum signatures, and the json/v2 graduation.
stories.why: More useful than the release notes: each feature ships with a working example plus links to the relevant CLs and proposals, and it flags the tradeoffs, such as interfaces still being unable to declare generic methods.
stories.takeaway: Go 1.27's center of gravity is the type system — generic methods and generalized function type inference land — alongside crypto/mldsa for post-quantum signatures and json/v2 becoming the default engine behind encoding/json.

stories.title: Postmortem for Lean Kernel Soundness Bug #14576
stories.dek: Lean's kernel had a soundness bug reachable via phantom parameters in nested inductive types; it surfaced through an AI-assisted 'disproof' of Collatz and was fixed within an hour.
stories.why: A rare inside look at the Lean FRO's incident response: what the bug was, why the independent nanoda checker also missed it (a second, unrelated bug), and why restricting metaprogramming is the wrong fix.
stories.takeaway: Soundness cannot depend on an untrusted elaborator refusing to build bad terms — the kernel must reject ill-typed declarations itself — and independent proof checkers only help if you keep both implementations current.

stories.title: LLMs won't break symmetric crypto
stories.dek: JP Aumasson on Anthropic's Mythos cryptanalysis results and why symmetric primitives are structurally resistant to LLM-driven attacks.
stories.why: Contextualizes the real results — HAWK-512 reduced from a 128-bit target to at most 108 bits, and an improved key recovery on 7-round AES-128 — and argues why full-round AES, SHA-3, and BLAKE3 remain safe.
stories.takeaway: Symmetric crypto's deliberate lack of mathematical structure (XOR and modular addition each destroy the other's structure) leaves mostly well-explored differential cryptanalysis, so LLM effort is better spent on underanalyzed post-quantum candidates.

stories.title: Apple Screen Sharing Pre-Auth RCE
stories.dek: A frame-length validation bug in screensharingd's SRP handler lets an unauthenticated attacker achieve root RCE; fixed in macOS 26.6.
stories.why: A detailed root-cause writeup: the 'frame too large' error path returns the stale success status of the preceding read, the caller treats it as authentication complete, and the cleartext session's root file-copy protocol does the rest.
stories.takeaway: Error-path hygiene in auth code matters: returning a stale success code on a validation failure skips the entire SRP key exchange and cipher install, handing pre-auth root file read/write — and crontabs must be mode 0600 or cron silently ignores them.
